questions.question: When vehicles are on both sides of your motorcycle, which lane position is usually safest?

options.text: Left
Right
Center

questions.correctAnswerText: Center
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best. A good rider changes position based on traffic and road conditions. When vehicles are on both sides, the center position is usually the safest.

questions.question: Locking your brakes can:

options.text: Be helpful in most situations.
Improve steering.
Cause control problems.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cause control problems.
questions.explanation: Locking the brakes can cause control problems. If your front brake locks, release it and re-apply it right away. If your rear brake locks on dry pavement, keep it locked until you stop.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Assume other drivers will yield to you.
Change your lane position to be more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position to be more visible.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move to the lane position where other drivers can see you best.

questions.question: To get the most protection from your helmet, make sure it:

options.text: Fits snugly.
Is clean.
Looks cool.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly.
questions.explanation: Your helmet will protect you best if it meets DOT standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no damage.

questions.question: Should you wear gloves while riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Yes. Your hands may get cold while riding.
Yes. They improve grip and protect your hands.
No. Gloves can interfere with the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes. They improve grip and protect your hands.
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip and protect your hands. Use full-fingered gloves made of durable material.

questions.question: Riding is difficult right after rain starts because:

options.text: Some drivers may not react quickly to the rain.
The pavement becomes very slippery.
Other drivers drive too slowly in wet weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pavement becomes very slippery.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, oil from vehicles has not yet washed away from the road. This oil mixes with water to create a slippery surface.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
Drivers may proceed through with caution.
Drivers must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red traffic light. You must stop completely and wait for a signal allowing you to turn.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Sneakers
Leather boots
Sandals

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather boots
questions.explanation: Leather boots provide the best protection. They should be high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: If you have one drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
It can affect your ability to ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect your ability to ride.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can harm your riding skills. Do not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to turn red.
The traffic light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns that the signal will change to red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through.

questions.question: Having just one alcoholic drink before riding:

options.text: Will not result in a DUI conviction.
Will never affect your riding skills.
Can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your riding ability. You can be charged with riding impaired even if your blood alcohol level is below the legal limit.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlights to tell the other vehicle to go.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: Your motorcycle should fit you, which means:

options.text: Your fingertips can barely touch the handlebars when seated.
The seat should be one foot higher than your waist when standing next to it.
Your feet should easily touch the ground when seated.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your feet should easily touch the ground when seated.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you well when your feet can easily touch the ground while you sit on it. Always check that a motorcycle fits before you ride it.

questions.question: When a motorcyclist needs to stop quickly, they should:

options.text: Use both brakes at the same time.
Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use both brakes at the same time. Look ahead at the road to help you avoid sudden stops.

questions.question: Which color will make you less visible to other drivers?

options.text: Orange
Yellow
Brown

questions.correctAnswerText: Brown
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green to be more visible to other drivers. Avoid dark or dull colors when riding.

questions.question: A sign that your rear tire has gone flat is:

options.text: The back of your motorcycle sways from side to side.
You hear a loud noise.
You see air coming out.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back of your motorcycle sways from side to side.
questions.explanation: When a rear tire goes flat, the back of the motorcycle may jerk or sway from side to side. If you feel this movement, stop and check your tires right away.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the roadside with its lights flashing. You should:

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait for the vehicle to start moving.
Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle with flashing lights, move to a different lane to give it space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Not change gears.
Shift up through the gears.
Shift down through the gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down through the gears.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: When starting your motorcycle, the engine should be in:

options.text: First gear.
Neutral.
Third gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Neutral.
questions.explanation: Make sure your motorcycle is in neutral before you start the engine. Most motorcycles have a light on the speedometer that shows when the bike is in neutral.

questions.question: The best way to avoid fatigue on a long motorcycle trip is to:

options.text: Take frequent breaks to rest.
Ride as fast as possible.
Take artificial stimulants.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take frequent breaks to rest.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on long trips, limit your daily riding time and take frequent rest breaks. Do not use artificial stimulants because you may crash when they wear off.
